Incineroar leads for Intimidate, Fake Out, and Parting Shot against the physical attackers. Kingambit handles Dragapult and Hydreigon with Dark attacks and has strong Steel coverage. Archaludon adds special pressure with Dracometeor and Electroshot against Gliscor and Milotic.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick 3 from our team against their dragon-heavy lineup with Garchomp, Dragapult, Kommo-o, Hydreigon, Gliscor, and Milotic. Incineroar looks strong with Intimidate and Fake Out utility, and Kingambit could hit hard against the Dragon/Ghost types since Dark is super effective on Dragapult.

I'm weighing Archaludon versus Gholdengo as the third pick, checking type matchups since Steel resists some but not all of their dragon coverage, and Gholdengo offers Shadow Ball value against Dragapult and Hydreigon despite Dark resisting it.

I'll settle on Incineroar leading, backed by Kingambit and Archaludon, since Archaludon's Draco Meteor hits dragon-types hard.

decisions.thought: 52% MOVE: earthquake, 17% MOVE: stoneedge, 14% MOVE: stealthrock

Incineroar is slower than Garchomp, so Garchomp would otherwise hit first. Fake Out has +3 priority, so it moves first, chips Garchomp, and flinches it for a turn. It is only usable on the first turn, so this is the moment to use it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Since Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar, Fake Out's priority lets it hit first anyway, flinching Garchomp and preventing its move while chipping some damage - that's clearly the strongest opening play here.

decisions.thought: 52% MOVE: earthquake, 14% MOVE: stoneedge, 13% MOVE: stealthrock

Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar, and Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragon. Parting Shot drops its Attack again, and the switch brings in Kingambit, which takes Outrage neutrally and handles Garchomp better than Archaludon, which Garchomp hits super effectively.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar at 86% health, and it's at -1 Attack, likely running Earthquake or Outrage. Flare Blitz would only be half-effective against Dragon, so I'm weighing whether to switch to Kingambit, which should take Garchomp's attacks reasonably well.

Checking type matchups though: Kingambit's Steel typing is actually weak to Ground, so Earthquake would hit it for 2x, and Archaludon as Steel/Dragon would also be weak to both Ground and Dragon moves, making both switches risky. Incineroar itself takes Dragon and Ground moves neutrally, so Parting Shot could be a good option to drop Garchomp's offenses further while pivoting into Kingambit or Archaludon safely, though that still leaves the switch-in vulnerable to Earthquake. Alternatively, Protect could let me scout Garchomp's move for free damage via Rough Skin avoidance while keeping Incineroar's health intact against the incoming hit.

decisions.thought: Incineroar fainted, so I must switch. Garchomp's Earthquake hits both options for super-effective damage, but Archaludon's Stamina raises its Defense when hit. Dracometeor is 2x on Garchomp and Archaludon has strong Special Attack, so it can threaten a big hit next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar down, I need to switch to either Kingambit or Archaludon against Garchomp's Life Orb Earthquake set. Archaludon is Steel/Dragon, so it's 4x weak to Ground, making that swap risky despite resisting Dragon-type moves.

Kingambit is also Ground-weak but hits back hard with Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave, while Archaludon's Electroshot would be immune against Garchomp's Ground typing anyway. Dracometeor would at least hit Garchomp super effectively for Dragon/Dragon coverage, and Archaludon's Stamina ability could let it gain a Defense boost if it eats an Earthquake, so I'm weighing which switch survives better given the speed and defensive stats on both sides.

Archaludon's Dracometeor with its 194 SpA should land a solid STAB super effective hit on Garchomp's already-weakened HP, so switching into Archaludon looks like the better play here.

decisions.thought: 64% MOVE: earthquake, 13% MOVE: stealthrock, 8% SWITCH: kommoo

Garchomp is Dragon/Ground, so Electro Shot does nothing and Flash Cannon is only neutral. Dracometeor is super effective, and Archaludon's Sp. Atk should deal well over Garchomp's remaining ~160 HP even with the drop. Even if Garchomp moves first with Earthquake, Archaludon should survive.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp at 76% HP with Life Orb and Rough Skin is Dragon/Ground, facing off against Archaludon which is Steel/Dragon. I'm working out the type matchup - Archaludon's Dragon-type moves would hit Garchomp super effectively since Dragon is weak to Dragon, but I need to check how Steel interacts with Garchomp's typing too, since Steel doesn't touch Dragon but does affect Ground.

Electroshot would be useless here since Ground types are immune to Electric, so Draco Meteor is clearly the best option with its 130 base power and the 2x STAB plus type effectiveness bonus. Running the numbers with Archaludon's 194 Special Attack against Garchomp's Special Defense, I'm calculating roughly 283 damage output, which far exceeds Garchomp's remaining HP and should secure the knockout. Now I'm considering the speed matchup and whether Garchomp could retaliate first with Earthquake, which would hit Archaludon's Steel typing for double damage.

decisions.thought: 39% MOVE: shadowball, 33% SWITCH: kommoo, 12% MOVE: dragontail

Dragapult outspeeds Archaludon, so it will likely strike first. Dracometeor is super effective (2x) and is the only option that can knock out Dragapult this turn, so I'll take the 90% accuracy risk. Flash Cannon and Electroshot do little here.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Archaludon at 64 HP is facing a faster Dragapult, so I need to check if Dracometeor's 130 base power, doubled for being super effective against the Dragon typing, can get through despite the harsh special attack drop it causes afterward.

It's a close call against Dragapult's bulk, and even if it lands, Dragapult likely strikes first with Dragon Darts or Phantom Force and could knock out my fragile Archaludon before I get the chance. I'm weighing whether switching to Kingambit is safer, though its Dark typing leaves it exposed to Dragapult's Ghost-type attacks.

Steel resists Dragon, so Archaludon as Steel/Dragon only takes neutral damage from Dragon moves overall, making it fairly sturdy against Dragapult's Dracometeor despite the self-stat drop.

Switching to Kingambit is another option since it resists both Dragon and Ghost and has solid bulk at 177 HP, but that costs Archaludon's remaining health. Dracometeor still seems like the better pick for pressuring Archaludon directly.

decisions.thought: Only one legal action is available: switching in Kingambit. Kingambit is the only healthy Pokémon left on my side, and it is the required replacement after Archaludon fainted.

Dragapult outspeeds Kingambit, so a normal attack would take a Shadow Ball first. Sucker Punch has +1 priority and Dark is super effective on Dragapult, so it should KO before Dragapult moves if Dragapult attacks. Dark STAB with Supreme Overlord and Black Glasses should be enough to KO even at the low end of its HP range.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragapult outspeeds Kingambit easily, and its Dragon/Ghost typing means Dark moves hit super effectively on the Ghost side. With two fainted allies boosting Supreme Overlord by 20%, Kowtow Cleave backed by Black Glasses and that power boost should hit hard.

Sucker Punch, though priority, needs Dragapult to use a non-status move to connect—against Shadow Ball it would work, but the damage output on paper looks slightly lower than a clean Kowtow Cleave since priority moves generally have lower base power. Either way, both options threaten serious damage given STAB and the double-super-effective-style multiplier from Dark into the Ghost-type half of Dragapult's typing.

Even at the low end, Sucker Punch's minimum damage still exceeds Dragapult's max HP, so it's a guaranteed KO if Dragapult attacks, and since priority lets it hit first, I'll go with Sucker Punch.

decisions.thought: 72% MOVE: focusblast, 19% MOVE: earthquake, 4% SWITCH: dragapult

Kommoo is Dragon/Fighting, so Kingambit's Dark and Steel attacks are both resisted. Kowtow Cleave is the strongest option: 85 power with Dark STAB, Black Glasses, and Supreme Overlord's +20% from two fainted allies. It also never misses. Sucker Punch is risky because it fails if Kommoo doesn't attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm calculating Kingambit's boosted attack with Supreme Overlord plus Black Glasses, then checking type effectiveness of Dark against Kommo-o's Dragon/Fighting typing, which looks neutral on both counts.

Checking Steel's effectiveness against Dragon, I'm recalling it's resisted at 0.5x, so Iron Head ends up at 0.5x total against Kommo-o, similar to Dark's resistance there.

Comparing Kowtow Cleave (85 BP, ignores accuracy, Dark STAB) versus Iron Head (80 BP, Steel STAB) — both land at the same effectiveness, but Kowtow Cleave's higher power and guaranteed accuracy with Black Glasses makes it the better pick for Kingambit. I'm also weighing whether Sucker Punch could work, though it fails if the target isn't attacking that turn, which is risky.

Swords Dance is tempting as a setup option since Kingambit's 177 HP gives it some bulk to survive, but with Kommoo likely being a physical attacker using moves like Clanging Scales or Dragon Claw, going straight for Kowtow Cleave seems like the safer, higher-value choice right now.
